reasons: No tests are visible in the packet.
The moments file path depends on the working folder.

terms.meaning: The library the app uses to talk to its database.
A database rule that stops two rows with the same values, here one lock per fan per moment.
Save a row, creating it if missing or updating it if it exists.
A fingerprint of file contents, used to prove which version of the data was used.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for file and database access
sections.what: Brings in file reading, path joining, the database client and the database error types. Users do not see this directly.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the imports.
sections.watch_out: Moving the database client file breaks every query in this file.

sections.name: StoredMoment, MomentsFile
sections.title: Shape of a stored golden moment
sections.what: Describes what is stored for each moment: match and season, the state before the decision, the choices with model win estimates, the reveal of the result, and the after-lock path, which exists only once a call is locked.
sections.why: Likely reason: one stored record holds both what fans see and what stays hidden until they lock.
sections.watch_out: Model estimates and the reveal are secret before lock, so anything that sends this type to a browser must remove them first.

sections.name: momentsFile
sections.title: Reads the golden moments file
sections.what: Reads and parses the committed moments file from the data folder and returns all of it, including its fingerprints. The service loads it and caches it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The file is committed and hashed, which suggests the results must be reproducible.
sections.watch_out: The path is relative to the working folder, so starting the app from another folder makes this fail.

sections.name: storedMoments
sections.title: List of stored moments
sections.what: Returns only the list of moments from the file.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its name.
sections.watch_out: Nothing is cached here, so each call reads the file again; the service adds caching.

sections.name: insertCall, reviewSelect, findCall
sections.title: Saving a lock and reading a call
sections.what: Saves a fan's locked pick with its confidence, and returns nothing if that fan already locked this moment. Also defines which review fields to read and fetches one fan's call for a moment.
sections.why: The database unique key on user and moment makes a second lock fail even when two requests race.
sections.watch_out: The duplicate check depends on the database rule, not on code, so the rule must stay in place.

sections.name: callsInLockOrder, ReviewRow, ReviewData
sections.title: A fan's calls in lock order
sections.what: Lists all of a fan's calls in the order they were locked, each with its review if graded, and defines the review row types.
sections.why: Ratings are built one call at a time, so the order matters.
sections.watch_out: Calls with the same lock time are ordered by id, which is stable but arbitrary.

sections.name: insertReview, calledMomentIds, deleteReviewsFor, deleteReviews, findCallForShare
sections.title: Saving reviews and reading share data
sections.what: Stores a review for a call, keeping the existing one if a concurrent write won. Also lists the moments a fan has called, deletes reviews, and fetches a call with the fan's display name for a share card.
sections.why: Two requests can grade the same call at once, and the first write wins.
sections.watch_out: The share lookup includes the fan's name, so any public view that uses it exposes that name.

sections.name: crowdCounts, displayName, shareTokenFor, userForShareToken, createShareToken, deleteShareToken
sections.title: Crowd counts and share token handling
sections.what: Counts other fans' picks per moment and option, looks up a display name, and creates, reads or deletes the random token for sharing an Alter Ego card. Creating a token for a fan who already has one keeps the old token.
sections.why: The comments say this supports the crowd comparison and opt-in sharing.
sections.watch_out: A new token passed in does not replace an existing one, so regenerating a link does nothing until the old token is deleted.

summary: The database and file access layer for the Decision Lab: reads the golden moments file, and reads and writes a fan's calls, reviews and share tokens.
purpose: Keeps all direct database queries for the Lab in one file, so the Lab rules in the service do not talk to the database directly.
why: Likely reason: separating storage from rules keeps the service testable and keeps database details in one place.
how: 1. Loads the golden moments JSON file from the data folder. 2. Inserts a call, and returns nothing when the fan already locked that moment. 3. Reads a call with its review. 4. Stores a review, keeping an existing one if a concurrent request already wrote it. 5. Counts other fans' picks per moment. 6. Creates, reads and deletes share tokens, and deletes reviews.
inputs: User ids, call ids, moment ids, and review data passed in from the service.
outputs: Stored moments from the file, call and review rows, counts, display names and share tokens.
risks: The moments file is read using a path relative to the working folder, so running from another folder fails. Deleting a user's reviews erases their graded history. A share token leads to the owner, so a leaked token exposes that fan's card.
debug: If moments are missing, check the working folder and that the golden moments file exists. If a lock fails unexpectedly, check the unique key on user and moment. If a review disappears, check the regrade path in the service.
